newsitem.title: GREECE: Papandreou feud turning into court-room drama.
newsitem.headline: Papandreou feud turning into court-room drama.

text.p: Efforts by Greece's ruling socialists to spare the memory of their founder Andreas Papandreou from a row between his blonde widow and his four children over his legacy were sunk by lawsuits this week.

A mysterious will found in a dusty old book in a cellar is sure to turn the Papandreou family feud, watched in Greece as closely as royal family squabbles in Britain, from a soap opera to a court-room drama.
At stake is the pink villa of Greece's controversial First Widow Dimitra Liani, an Olympic Airways flight attendant who became Papandreou's wife and chief of staff.

"It's a pity that lawsuits seal the failure of an effort to have an understanding between Papandreou's widow and children," the daily Ta Nea said in its main editorial. "His memory deserved better; not to be dragged through the courts."

The revered socialist leader sold his mother's house for a reported $800,000 to build a luxurious house for Liani, who was about half his age when they met as she served him drinks on an airliner in 1988.
But a will by Papandreou's mother, recently discoverd by his daughter Sofia, leaves the suburban Athens house to the four children, who are suing to have the sale reversed.
The children say they want to turn the house, where Papandreou was arrested before their eyes at the start of a seven-year dictatorship in 1967, into an institute devoted to his memory.
The socialist party, which had tried to settle the headline-grabbing dispute quietly before long-simmering tensions exploded, has thrown in the towel.

"This issue, everything that precedes it and everything that might follow, some of which is unpleasant, cannot mar the memory of Andreas Papandreou," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters.

More than 100 socialist deputies appealed in a statement last week to all concerned to show respect for his memory. The party even persuaded Liani and the children to sign a joint statement denying that they were bickering over the design of Papandreou's gravestone.

The children, who had been discreet about Liani while their father was alive, have openly expressed their distaste in recent months -- Papandreou's son Nikos described her to a Western newspaper as a "power-hungry vulture".
Papandreou's eldest son and deputy foreign minister George has not joined the others in the suit but has defended their right to claim the historic home.
Liani's meteoric rise, unpolished ways and published nude sunbathing pictures never gained her much public sympathy, while her pink villa was difficult to explain to a public suffering a recession.
Those close to her say she built the house as life insurance after Papandreou, knowing her political aspirations would end and high-powered friends would leave after his death.
The flamboyant Greek socialist party founder married Liani in 1989 after a public extra-marital affair that partly cost him an election defeat in 1989 after eight years in power.

He weathered that, scandals and a tripple by-pass operation and returned to power in 1993 with Liani at his side. He was urgently hospitalised in November last year, resigned as prime minister two months later and died at home in June.
